walkthrough.webnb.output: How the demo notes server works The next few steps read through demo-src/server.js, a tiny HTTP API that stores notes in memory, and then peek at its helpers. 1 Setup The file starts by pulling in Node's http module and two helpers, then sets up the server's state. This snippet is anchored by the #region setup marker in the file, so it keeps working even when the file grows. demo-src/server.js setup · lines 5–10 5 const http = require('http'); 6 const { readBody, sendJson } = require('./utils'); 7 8 const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000; 9 const notes = new Map(); All the notes live in this Map, keyed by id — restart the server and they are gone. 10 let nextId = 1; Ids are handed out from a simple counter. 2 Routing All routing happens in one function: check the method and URL, handle the match, and fall through to a 404. demo-src/server.js routes · lines 14–27 14 async function handleRequest(request, response) { 15 if (request.method === 'GET' && request.url === '/notes') { Listing notes is just serializing the map's values. 16 return sendJson(response, 200, Array.from(notes.values())); 17 } 18 19 if (request.method === 'POST' && request.url === '/notes') { 20 const body = await readBody(request); The request body is parsed before the note is created. Everything after this line can assume body is a plain object. 21 const note = { id: nextId++, text: body.text }; 22 notes.set(note.id, note); 23 return sendJson(response, 201, note); 24 } 25 26 sendJson(response, 404, { error: 'Not found' }); 27 } 3 Starting up Finally the server is created and started. demo-src/server.js startup · lines 31–39 31 const server = http.createServer((request, response) => { 32 handleRequest(request, response).catch(error => { Any error thrown by a route handler is turned into a JSON 500 response here, so one bad request cannot crash the server. 33 sendJson(response, 500, { error: error.message }); 34 }); 35 }); 36 37 server.listen(PORT, () => { 38 console.log(`Notes API listening on port ${PORT}`); 39 }); 4 The helpers This step uses explicit lines: ranges instead of region markers, so the two helpers show with a gap between them. demo-src/utils.js lines 3–18, 20–23 3 function readBody(request) { 4 return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { 5 let raw = ''; 6 request.on('data', chunk => { 7 raw += chunk; 8 }); 9 request.on('end', () => { 10 try { 11 resolve(raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : {}); 12 } catch (error) { 13 reject(new Error('Body must be valid JSON')); If the body is not valid JSON, the promise rejects and the routing layer turns it into an error response. 14 } 15 }); 16 request.on('error', reject); 17 }); 18 } ⋯ 20 function sendJson(response, status, payload) { 21 response.writeHead(status, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); 22 response.end(JSON.stringify(payload)); 23 } sendJson is the only place that writes to the response, which keeps the content-type header consistent everywhere. 5 One line A step can be as small as a single line. Both helpers leave through this one export. demo-src/utils.js line 25 25 module.exports = { readBody, sendJson };
